TV host Dr. Phil McGraw opened up about 50 crashed UFO aircraft and mentioned that these retained spacecrafts were made with metallurgical substances, an element not present on Earth. While speaking at the American Thought Leaders interview, Dr. Phil said,

"They're made up of metallurgical substances that we don't have on this planet."

McGraw mentioned that he got this information from his trusted credible sources and explained that the United States possesses spacecraft that are not of human origin.

The TV host further explained that these UFO aircraft either crashed or landed and were then recovered by the government. Dr. Phil recalled that when he asked the sources about the number of crashed spacecraft, they revealed that there were more than 50 crashed aircraft.

Continue reading more about 50 crashed UFO aircraft.

American Thought Leaders interview: Dr. Phil McGraw revealed details about 50 crashed UFO aircraft

During the interview, McGraw revealed that sources had told him about 50 crashed UFO aircraft. After these spacecrafts were recovered, it was revealed that they were made up of metallurgical substances that are not present on Earth. Dr. Phil revealed,

"I am told by credible people that I have confidence in that we do have spacecraft that have either crashed or landed and been retained in our possession."

He added,

"They're saying that they're made up of metallurgical substances that we don't have on this planet."

However, two years ago, News Nation revealed that the Pentagon's UFO office released a report and mentioned that a piece of metal linked to a UAP most likely came from Earth.

Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) in Tennessee studied the sample and revealed that the metal was not extraterrestrial. However, some people claimed that it was a special alloy not found on Earth and had the ability to act as a terahertz waveguide to create antigravity effects.

ORNL also revealed that it could not confirm the exact history of the sample because the chain of custody was unclear. However, the lab noted that the material matches the kind of scientific experiments carried out during that period.

The Roswell incident revealed crashed UFO aircraft

In 1947, rancher William Brazel found strange debris near his ranch outside Roswell, New Mexico. At that time, the country was caught up in a flying saucer craze, but William didn't know about it because he had no phone or radio. After he reported the discovery to the local sheriff, the sheriff contacted the U.S. Air Force.

The Air Force then issued an initial press release and said that the military had recovered debris from a flying disc. Later, the Air Force withdrew the statement and explained that the debris actually came from a regular weather balloon.

In 1978, a retired officer said the weather balloon claim was a cover-up and suggested that the debris was of alien origin. The rumor started a conspiracy that lasted for decades.

In 1994, the Air Force released a report and confirmed that the weather balloon story was indeed a cover-up, but not about aliens. The debris actually came from Project Mogul, a classified program that tested high-altitude balloons, which was what William found on his ranch.
